title: Caracol
summary: Caracol, on the Vaca Plateau of western Belize, was a large Classic Maya city with a population of over 100,000 at its height. It defeated Tikal in 562 CE and Naranjo in 631. Its central complex, Caana, still rises about 43.5 m above its plaza and is the tallest man-made structure in Belize.

uncertainty.note: The Caracol Archaeological Project gives the Classic era as AD 250-950; Chase and Chase (Springer) give AD 250-900 and place first settlement at about 600 BC, so the range covers the Classic era only, not the earlier occupation.

where.historical_name: Caracol (ancient Oxwitza'), Classic Maya city-state in the southern lowlands

importance.justification: Largest Classic Maya site in Belize, whose AD 562 war against Tikal reshaped lowland politics; Caana is its monumental core.
